candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items), within Safe and Effective Care Environment; this item tests effective collaboration with another regulated health professional without transferring nursing accountability or inventing a universal state-law scope.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Understanding respiratory-therapy responsibilities within interdisciplinary care
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize respiratory therapists as direct-care interdisciplinary clinicians whose model practice scope includes prescribed respiratory therapies, monitoring treatment response, diagnostic activities, and certain emergency procedures within applicable legal authority.

options.A: Administering prescribed respiratory-care agents and monitoring the client's response to respiratory treatment and diagnostic testing
options.B: Independently prescribing any medication without a physician order or other authority defined by law
options.C: Limiting practice to equipment maintenance without direct client assessment or treatment
options.D: Avoiding initiation of emergency respiratory procedures even when permitted by applicable regulations

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The AARC Model Practice Act states that respiratory-care practice includes administration of pharmacologic, diagnostic, and therapeutic agents related to respiratory care and observing and monitoring signs, symptoms, physical response, and other responses to respiratory treatment and diagnostic testing. The model language also allows initiation of emergency procedures under applicable board regulations or other authority. B overstates autonomous prescribing authority, while C and D contradict the described practice scope.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current AARC model legislation directly supports RT participation in respiratory therapies, monitoring and diagnostic care, while conditioning practice authority on orders, regulations, and state law rather than granting unlimited independent prescribing.
candidate.source_locator: AARC Model Practice Act → definition 3, 'Practice of Respiratory Care': includes administration of pharmacological, diagnostic and therapeutic agents related to respiratory-care procedures; observing and monitoring signs, symptoms, general behavior and physical response to respiratory treatment and diagnostic testing; appropriate reporting/referral/protocol-based changes pursuant to authorized orders; and initiation of emergency procedures under board regulations or otherwise permitted by the Act.
candidate.stem: A nurse collaborates with a respiratory therapist (RT) in caring for a client with respiratory disease. Which activity is explicitly included in the AARC Model Practice Act description of respiratory care practice?
